title: Biblical Greek: from the alphabet to 1 John 1
text: NA27 words as built in orig/nt (STEPBible TAGNT)
note: Hand-written lesson plan. vocab lists Strong's numbers from vocab.json (each lemma taught once, in frequency order within a lesson). exampleRefs are references only: verse text is read from orig/ at display time. No Greek is typed here; paradigm tables live in paradigms.json, the alphabet in alphabet.json.

lessons.title: The alphabet, part 1: alpha to mu
goals: Recognize and name the first twelve Greek letters, capital and small.
Say each one with its Erasmian sound, using the English sound-alikes.
Write each letter in the course transliteration.

lessons.title: The alphabet, part 2: nu to omega
goals: Recognize and name the last twelve letters, including the final form of sigma.
Tell apart letters that look like English letters but sound different (eta, nu, rho, chi, omega).
Sound out a short verse letter by letter.

lessons.title: Vowels, diphthongs and breathing marks
goals: Know the seven vowels and which are always long, always short, or either.
Read the eight diphthongs as single sounds.
Hear the rough breathing as h and ignore the smooth one; read past the iota subscript.

lessons.title: Accents, punctuation and reading aloud
goals: Recognize the three accents and stress the accented syllable when reading.
Read the raised dot as a pause and the semicolon-shaped mark as a question mark.
Spot elision and the movable nu, then read 1 John 1:1 aloud slowly.

lessons.title: First words: and, but, for, not, in
goals: Learn the small words that hold most sentences together.
Read the names Jesus and Christ.
Find these words in verses of John and 1 John.

lessons.title: Nouns and their cases: the second declension
goals: Understand that a Greek noun changes its ending to show its job in the sentence (case).
Learn the four cases: nominative (subject), genitive (of), dative (to/for/in), accusative (object).
Decline the word for word, logos, in singular and plural.
lessons.grammarTopic: Case, number and gender; second declension masculine

lessons.title: The article: the
goals: Learn all the forms of the article and use them to identify case, number and gender.
See that Greek has no word for a or an.
Decline a second declension neuter noun, where subject and object look the same.
lessons.grammarTopic: The definite article; second declension neuter

lessons.title: The first declension: life, day, glory
goals: Decline feminine nouns of the first declension in their three patterns.
Recognize the masculine first-declension nouns such as disciple and prophet.
Read the word for life in 1 John 1:1–2.
lessons.grammarTopic: First declension (eta, alpha and mixed types; masculine)

lessons.title: Verbs: the present active indicative
goals: See how a verb ending shows person and number, so the subject pronoun is often left out.
Learn the six present active endings.
Read short sentences with have, say, hear and write.

lessons.title: The verb to be: eimi
goals: Learn the present of the verb to be, which takes a nominative on both sides.
Recognize the imperfect was, the first verb in 1 John 1:1.
Add four common adverbs: now, then, again, thus.

lessons.title: Personal pronouns: I, you, he, she, it
goals: Learn the pronouns I/we and you, with their emphatic and unemphatic forms.
Learn autos as he/she/it, and recognize its other uses (self, same).
Read the we, us and you that run through 1 John 1.

lessons.title: Prepositions and the cases they take
goals: Learn twelve more prepositions.
See that the case after a preposition changes its meaning (with + genitive, after + accusative).
Read prepositional phrases in John and 1 John.
lessons.grammarTopic: Prepositions with genitive, dative and accusative; elided forms

lessons.title: Connecting words: if, as, therefore, or
goals: Learn the common conjunctions and particles that link clauses.
Notice that some, like de and gar, never come first in their clause.
Read short verses built from known words.

lessons.title: Adjectives
goals: See that an adjective takes the case, number and gender of its noun.
Tell an attributive adjective (the holy one) from a predicate one (is holy) by the article.
Recognize the forms of all, every, which appear twice in 1 John 1.
lessons.grammarTopic: Adjectives: agreement, attributive and predicate position

lessons.title: This, that, who and which
goals: Learn the demonstratives this and that.
Learn the relative pronoun who/which, which opens 1 John 1:1.
Tell the question word who? from the indefinite someone.
lessons.grammarTopic: Demonstrative, relative, interrogative and indefinite pronouns

lessons.title: Contract verbs: do, love, speak
goals: See how verbs whose stem ends in a vowel blend that vowel with the ending.
Recognize the contracted we-forms in 1 John 1 (we testify, we do, we deceive).
Learn six common contract verbs.
lessons.grammarTopic: Contract verbs (epsilon and alpha), present indicative

lessons.title: Middle and passive endings; deponent verbs
goals: Learn the present middle/passive endings.
Understand deponent verbs: middle or passive in form, active in meaning (I come, I become).
Recognize we lie in 1 John 1:6.

lessons.title: The third declension: father, flesh, name
goals: Find the stem of a third-declension noun from its genitive.
Learn the endings through three patterns.
Recognize father, hands, light and blood in 1 John 1.

lessons.title: More nouns: faith, city, nations, people
goals: Learn twelve frequent nouns, mostly third declension.
Read the names Paul, Peter and the word Jew.
Practise finding the stem from the genitive.

lessons.title: The aorist: what happened (recognition)
goals: Recognize the aorist, the simple past, by its augment (e- at the front) and sa endings.
Recognize second aorists such as said, and the aorist passive marked by thē.
Spot the three aorists in 1 John 1:1–2 (we looked at, they touched, was revealed).
lessons.grammarTopic: Aorist active, middle and passive indicative (recognition)

lessons.title: Give, hand over, stand, forgive
goals: Learn four common verbs whose dictionary form ends in -mi.
See that forgive in 1 John 1:9 is one of them.
Recognize them by their stems rather than by full tables.

lessons.title: The perfect: what has happened (recognition)
goals: Recognize the perfect, a past act with a lasting result, by its repeated first syllable and (usually) ka endings.
Read we have heard and we have seen, the perfects of 1 John 1:1–3.
Learn oida, perfect in form but present in meaning: I know.
lessons.grammarTopic: Perfect active indicative; perfect passive participle (recognition)

lessons.title: If and so that: the subjunctive (recognition)
goals: Recognize the subjunctive by its long linking vowel (long o, long e).
Read ean (if) and hina (so that) with the subjunctive, the backbone of 1 John 1:6–10.
Recognize the subjunctive of to be in 1 John 1:4.
lessons.grammarTopic: Present and aorist subjunctive with ean and hina (recognition)

lessons.title: Reading 1 John 1:1–10
goals: Read 1 John 1:1–10 in Greek with help for the words not yet learned.
Identify case, tense and person in each verse using the earlier lessons.
Follow the passage from what was heard and seen (1–4) to walking in the light (5–7) and confessing sin (8–10).
